questions: If the bottom row becomes completely filled after some blocks have moved downward during a time step, does the removal of the entire bottom row happen before or after those downward moves?
When the bottom row is removed, are the blocks that were just removed considered “existing” at the intermediate time T+0.5 for that same time step?

If multiple columns become empty after removal, does the removal affect only the blocks that were originally in the bottom row at the start of the step, or also blocks that moved into the bottom row during that step?

In the rule “If the block is in the bottom row, or if there is a block in the cell immediately below it, do nothing,” does “bottom row” refer to row 1 (y = 1) or row 0, and is the grid indexed from 1?
Are the coordinates (X_i, Y_i) given with Y increasing upward from the bottom, and does “bottom row” correspond to Y = 1?
When a block is removed because the bottom row is cleared, is its index A_j still considered valid for future queries, or should queries about that block always answer “No”?
If two blocks are stacked in the same column with a gap between them, does the upper block fall only one cell per time step, even if the gap is larger than one?
Are the time steps discrete such that the state at time T+0.5 is defined as after the removal step but before the next downward‑movement step, or vice versa?

inline_prompts: There is a grid with 10^9 rows and W columns. The cell at the x-th column from the left and the y-th row from the bottom is denoted by (x,y). There are N blocks. Each block is a 1 \times 1 square, and block i-th (1 \leq i \leq N) is located at cell (X_i,Y_i) at time 0. At times t=1,2,\dots,10^{100}, the blocks are moved according to the following rules: - If the entire bottom row is filled with blocks, then all blocks in the bottom row are removed. - For each remaining block, perform the following: - If the block is in the bottom row, or if there is a block in the cell immediately below it, do nothing. - Otherwise, move the block one cell downward. Related — processing is sequential bottom-to-top within a step, which bears on move/removal ordering. You are given Q queries. For the j-th query (1 \leq j \leq Q), answer whether block A_j exists at time T_j+0.5. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N W X_1 Y_1 X_2 Y_2 \vdots X_N Y_N Q T_1 A_1 T_2 A_2 \vdots T_Q A_Q Output Print Q lines. The i-th line should contain Yes if block A_i exists at time T_i+0.5, and No otherwise. Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq W \leq N - 1 \leq X_i \leq W - 1 \leq Y_i \leq 10^9 - (X_i,Y_i) \neq (X_j,Y_j) if i \neq j. - 1 \leq Q \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq T_j \leq 10^9 - 1 \leq A_j \leq N - All input values are integers.
